items.item: IRS correspondence arriving before the payment due date after an early filing (taxreturn.ts armCollection / nextNotice, COLLECTION.noticeWeeks after filing); Connecticut's equivalent
items.requirement: Tax shown on a return is due at the time fixed for filing it, without assessment or notice and demand (IRC 6151(a), read at law.cornell.edu 2026-10-16). Notice and demand follows an assessment, within 60 days of it (IRC 6303(a)); a levy is lawful only once the tax is unpaid 10 days after notice and demand (6331(a)) and after 30 days' written notice of intent (6331(d)(2)). Interest and the failure-to-pay penalty run only from the due date (6601(a), 6651(a)(2)). The IRS's published sequence is a first bill (CP14, 'If you owe taxes, we will send you a bill. This is your first bill for tax due'), at least one more bill, a final bill, then collection (IRS Publication 594, Rev. 1-2026, read 2026-10-16); the IRM puts the assessment (23C) date and the first notice date on the Monday of the third week after Master File posting (IRM 3.30.123.5.5, read 2026-10-16). So a balance-due bill (CP14) after processing is valid for a return filed early, naming the due date; a reminder that the balance is overdue (CP501 'you still owe it, with the interest and penalty since'), a second reminder (CP503), a notice of intent to levy (CP504) or a final notice (LT11) before the due date is premature. Whether the IRS holds an early return's CP14 until the due date wasn't found (uncertainty recorded). Connecticut: a tax 'due and unpaid' (Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-734) is collected on failure to pay 'within thirty days of its due date' (12-35(a)(2), (a)(3)), with notice 'not less than thirty days before the day the warrant is to be issued' for a bank account (12-35(b)(1)); read at codes.findlaw.com 2026-10-16.

items.item: The passport's lifecycle: eligibility, application, fee and time, issue and term, renewal, loss and replacement, and what a missing or expired one does
items.requirement: Each issuer's own rule for where the applicant is. A US citizen in the US renews by mail on Form DS-82 for $130 where the most recent passport was issued within the last 15 years, at 16 or older, valid for 10 years, never reported lost or stolen and undamaged (travel.state.gov 'Renew Your Passport by Mail', read 2026-10-16 through search; fee $130 in State's fee chart 'Updated October 2026', read through search 2026-10-16); otherwise Form DS-11, $130 and the $35 acceptance fee. A British national in the US applies from overseas: £116.50 online (gov.uk 'New fees for passport applications', published 18 March 2026, effective 8 April 2026, read 2026-10-16), and can't use the urgent Fast Track service ('You cannot use this service if you’re outside the UK', gov.uk/get-a-passport-urgently, read 2026-10-16). The other offices' rules from abroad as content/passports.ts's research of 2026-09-29 recorded them (`abroad`).
items.currentBehavior: documents.apply_passport (documents.ts:314-331) charges every applicant the office's domestic fee (passportTerms, :411-414) and offers its expedite (:417-424), wherever they apply from. Every life is in New Haven, so a citizen of any other country applies from abroad: a London-born student pressing Renew It is charged the UK's £102 domestic fee and offered Renew It Faster, the UK's Fast Track (£192, 7 days), which isn't sold outside the UK; Papers shows the office's 'From abroad' text beside it, which says £116.50 (Documents.tsx:132) — the screen contradicts the charge. A US citizen renewing pays $165 (DS-11's $130 + $35) where DS-82 is $130. Loss: documents.report_lost (:333-349) cancels it; no replacement path besides applying again (correct: a lost passport is replaced by a new application). What a missing or expired one does: photoIdOf (a new bank), ssnRefusal (the SSA) — and nothing at the DMV for a non-citizen (tax.s8.idcard).

items.item: The state ID card's lifecycle (Connecticut's non-driver identification card) and the documents it requires
items.requirement: Connecticut DMV's checklist (DI-3 Rev. 6-2026, 'REAL ID Document Identity Verification Checklist', read 2026-10-16 at portal.ct.gov): 'valid/unexpired, original documents'; two identity documents, one primary, a non-US-born applicant's primary being a foreign passport with its supporting documents ('F1 requires I-20 and I-94'), a Permanent Resident Card or an Employment Authorization Document (I-766), among others; the Social Security number or the SSA's ineligibility letter; two proofs of Connecticut residency; legal status checked through SAVE, ten business days or more; 'If you are not eligible for a verified REAL ID driver’s license or ID card, you will be issued a non-verified (Not for Federal Identification) driver’s license or ID card', and only US citizens and permanent residents are eligible for a verified one (portal.ct.gov, Drivers License Non-US Citizen Requirements, read 2026-10-16). The card costs $28 and is valid for seven years, and a new-issue card is processed at a DMV office and mailed within 20 business days (portal.ct.gov/dmv 'Get a non-driver ID', read 2026-10-16).
items.currentBehavior: idCardRefusal (identity.ts:80-117) for somebody not a citizen asks lawful presence (an F-1 at school or a US permit), the number, and none held or pending; it never asks for a passport, so a London-born student at school who reported her passport lost (documents.report_lost, reachable on Papers) after her Social Security card came is issued the card with no primary identity document. documents.apply_idcard (:223-244) marks a non-citizen's Limited Term card realId: true (:238), and the look says 'It meets REAL ID.' (looks/papers.tsx:208), where Connecticut issues a non-citizen with temporary status a non-verified card. A citizen's card is in force at once (:242) and runs six years (content/identity.ts:59), where DMV mails it within 20 business days and gives seven: recorded, not changed (below).
items.plan: (1) A non-citizen at a US state's counter needs a primary identity document in force: their passport (with the I-20 and I-94 an F-1 student at school holds), or a US permit in force (OPT's EAD); without one the DMV refuses and says to renew or replace the passport on Papers. (2) A non-citizen's card isn't REAL ID: realId false, and its look says Not For Federal Identification. (3) The citizen's mailing (20 business days) and seven-year term: recorded as an uncertainty and a finding, not changed here (a citizen's card in force at once is what tests/evidence-g15-papers.test.ts's verified journey asserts; whether DMV hands a temporary credential a bank accepts meanwhile wasn't found).
